fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Micah 6:16 says the city kept those statutes and followed that counsel. Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD (1 Kings 16:25), and so did his son Ahab (1 Kings 16:30). So the city was walking a road those two had already laid out.

Not this time, friend. Micah 6:16 has no tearing down and no burning in it. It says the city kept the statutes and followed the counsel. Omri and his son Ahab each did evil in the sight of the LORD (1 Kings 16:25, 30), so holding on to their ways was no small thing.

I wish that were so, baker, but verse 16 says otherwise. The city kept those practices and followed that counsel, so nothing had slipped its mind. Ahab reigned in the place of his father Omri (1 Kings 16:28), and the city was still following the ways of both. Those old habits were very much alive.
